back: A fault is one component deviating from its spec. A failure is the whole system no longer serving users. Fault tolerance stops faults becoming failures.
Any component whose failure on its own takes the whole service down. Find them by walking one request hop by hop.
Config and feature-flag stores, TLS certificates, one DNS provider, a shared auth service, and the one engineer who knows the failover steps.
One cause taking out many redundant copies at once: same zone, same deploy, same poison input, same dependency, same expiry date.
A request that crashes any instance that handles it. Load-balancer and client retries carry it to every copy. Defend with input limits and capped retries.
N+1 survives one failure. N+2 also survives a failure while one instance is out for a deploy or maintenance. For N = 6, N+2 costs about 33% extra.
Keeping the core job working with reduced quality when an optional dependency fails, instead of failing the whole request.

front: Availability gain from making 3 of 5 dependencies optional (each 99.9%)?

back: Drop the feature, serve a generic default, serve stale data, accept now and finish later via a queue, switch off expensive work, go read-only.
Fail open: treat an unavailable check as passed (rate limiters, recommendations). Fail closed: treat it as failed (authentication, payment authorisation).

front: Why can a fallback cause the outage?
back: It switches to a rarely used path during the worst conditions, often sending load to a system never sized for it (e.g. 100,000 reads/s onto a database sized for 200).

front: Safer alternatives to a fallback that calls another system?
back: Make the primary more reliable, make the fallback the normal path (local copy refreshed in background), or degrade by doing less.
A system that keeps working through a dependency failure without having to make any changes in response (AWS term).
Data plane serves each request (running instances, load balancer). Control plane changes the system (launch, scale, reconfigure). Static stability needs only the data plane during failure.

front: Statically stable capacity across N zones?
back: Provision 1 ÷ (N − 1) extra: 50% with 3 zones, 33% with 4. Losing one zone then needs no new instances.
